reviewStandard: Current identity, canonical route, rank, controlled identifier, nomenclatural standing, type evidence, conservative morphology, source-use licensing, and every cited DOI/title/PMID mapping were checked before prompt creation. All six current identities cleared for one immutable built-in call each. Five outputs remain review candidates. The Phocaeicola output was rejected and quarantined after fail-closed scrutiny: the 2009 type-species description reports lophotrichous flagella, but the 2019 expanded current-genus reassessment materially questions whether those structures were flagella rather than exopolysaccharide, and the rendered tufts contain four rather than the requested three filaments. Every PNG was inspected at original 1536 by 1024 resolution. Observed bodies, spatial groupings, major structures, background treatment, cover safety, and deviations are literal native-resolution audit results; prompt counts are not output evidence. The five candidates remain review-only and require separate Control Tower exact-hash acceptance before promotion.

A conspicuously flagellated genus plate therefore overstates unsettled morphology.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI Taxonomy and Index Fungorum retain Penicillium as current genus NCBITaxon:5073 and Index Fungorum:9257, with Penicillium expansum as type species. The modern genus treatment is PMID 25505353, PMCID PMC4261876, DOI 10.1016/j.simyco.2014.09.001, and supports septate hyphae and brush-like penicilli bearing conidial chains. The plate is type-species anchored, representative, non-universal, and non-diagnostic.
assets.visualReview: One connected basal septate hyphal grouping supports exactly two upright conidiophores. Each conidiophore ends in one compact brush-like penicillus composed of restrained branches and multiple attached round conidial chains. Every visible conidium remains attached; there is no free spore cloud. No colony, substrate, fruit, plant, host tissue, label, text, scale bar, decorative particle, scenery, clipping, signature, or watermark is visible.
